knowledge_point.title: Differentiating a Logarithmic Function With a General Base

question.:question/worked-solution:
To differentiate a logarithm with base $a,$ we use the formula

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\log_a x)=\frac{1}{x\ln a}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x-4\log_{9}x) \\ & =1-4\cdot \frac{1}{x\ln 9} \\ & =1 - \frac{4}{x \ln{\left(9 \right)}}.\end{aligned}
$$

generation.domain: x>0; logarithm base positive and unequal to1; integer base2..12

To differentiate a logarithm with base $a,$ we use the formula

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\log_{a}x)=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}a}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{'}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\log_{10}x-8\operatorname{ln}x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\log_{10}x)-8\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}x) \\  & =\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}(10)}-8(\frac{1}{x}) \\  & =\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}(10)}-\frac{8}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

generation.domain: x>0; logarithm base positive and unequal to1; integer base2..12

question.:question/problem:
Given the function $y=2{x}^{3}+x-3{log}_{6}⁡x,$ find the instantaneous rate of change at $x=3.$ Do not round the answer.

The instantaneous rate of change at $x=3$ is
{{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
To differentiate a logarithm with base $a,$ we use the formula

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({log}_{a}⁡x)=\frac{1}{xln⁡a}.
$$

To find the instantaneous rate of change at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{3}+x-3{log}_{6}⁡x) \\  & =2\cdot 3{x}^{2}+1-3\cdot \frac{1}{xln⁡6} \\  & =6{x}^{2}+1-\frac{3}{xln⁡6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate of change at $x=3$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=3} & ={(6{x}^{2}+1-\frac{3}{xln⁡6})|}_{x=3} \\  & =6(3)^{2}+1-\frac{3}{3\cdot ln⁡6} \\  & =55-\frac{1}{ln⁡6}\,.\end{aligned}
$$
